params.body:
## What

A story now looks like the other pages of the site instead of a frame page.

- **Top:** on white, the title, lead and date on the left and the image on the right. It reuses the photo and text block from Over ons (`rb-photo-text`, photo right). Vergroten still opens the image.
- **Below:** the story in one reading column (the existing `.article__body`, 720px), in the type of the photo and text block: 15px, line height 1.7, headings 22px. The gallery, lists and FAQ block sit in that column. Then the two buttons, the frames and more stories.
- **Phone:** the image first, then title and text.

## Why

The frame-page layout (`.fd`) kept the image in view on the left and put the whole story in the narrow right column, on a beige ground. That works for a frame's few lines. For an article of five sections it gave a long, cramped column next to an empty half of the page, in a look the rest of the site does not use.

## Checked

- Full suite: 484 tests, 483 pass. `BuildStampTest` fails in any git worktree, also on main. Pint passes.
- `StoriesTest` and `BlogTest` assert the new head, back link and body column.
- Looked at locally on desktop and mobile with the two published stories (H8 & F8, Repair Kit) in four languages.
params.title: Lay out a story like the site's photo and text pages
